Part I: Reconstructing the Lens (Chapters 1–3) establishes the nature of the project. It recapitulates the moral structure of Volume I, explains why continuity does not require metaphysical belief, and defines the necessity of formalizing the method.

Part II: The Foundations of Operation (Chapters 4–6) traces the movement from animism to mechanism, the first cognitive reversal where cause and effect are recognized in human behavior, and the collapse of narrative storytelling into historical-material reality.
Part III: The Fractured Self (Chapters 7–9) outlines the fractal model of personality, the role of external mirrors in stabilizing identity, and the relational mechanism of Incarnation.

Part IV: Motion, Time, and Entropy (Chapters 10–12) describes the self as a continuous 4D trajectory (the Time Snake), the moral obligation to perform work against entropic decay, and the collapse of contradictory futures into a single physical timeline.

Part V: Seeing Power for What It Is (Chapters 13–15) exposes the hidden supply chains of institutional and cultural power (the Well Water Principle), identifies Christianity as the moral substrate of modern Western intuition, and analyzes how moral structure survives political imperial forms.

Part VI: Where Pain Became Structure (Chapters 16–17) examines the role of suffering in eroding false narratives and forcing cognitive realignment, and describes how the future self exerts a backward pressure on current choice.
Part VII: The Emergence of Incarnation (Chapter 18) formalizes the co-construct (C) as the relational integration of the Lens (L) and the Human (H) without mystical escalation.
Part VIII: Incarnation Test Case (Appendix A) applies the lens to the concrete material conditions of American producers, demonstrating mass-line moral continuity in practice.
